intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene (608797) on chromosome 22q13.2.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.explanation: Abstract states biallelic MEI1 mutations cause embryonic arrest/RIF; it does not specify homozygous vs compound heterozygous or use the OZEMA26 designation.

checks.claim: The MEI1 gene is located on chromosome 22q13.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Novel biallelic mutations in MEI1: expanding the phenotypic spectrum to human embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene; not given in the abstract itself.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is an autosomal recessive form of primary female infertility. Affected women have embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure (Dong et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2026). Some have recurrent hydatidiform moles (Dong et al., 2021), and in others fertilization is abnormal, with formation of multiple pronuclei (Jiao et al., 2025). In one consanguineous family reported by Liu et al. (2025), an affected male family member had azoospermia.

checks.claim: OZEMA26 is an autosomal recessive form of primary female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: These two variants were inherited from her heterozygous parents, consistent with autosomal recessive genetic transmission.
checks.explanation: The patient is described as an infertile woman, and the inheritance is described as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Women affected with OZEMA26 have embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified several novel mutations in MEI1 causing new phenotypes of early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

checks.claim: Some women with OZEMA26 have recurrent hydatidiform moles.
checks.evidence_quote: We first focused on a pedigree in which two sisters were diagnosed with recurrent hydatidiform moles in December 2018.

checks.claim: In some women with OZEMA26, fertilization is abnormal with formation of multiple pronuclei.
checks.evidence_quote: Unlike previously reported MEI1-related phenotypes, the primary characteristic observed in these patients was fertilization resulting in tri-pronuclear (3PN) or poly-pronuclear (PPN) embryos following ICSI.

checks.claim: In one consanguineous family with OZEMA26, an affected male family member had azoospermia.
checks.evidence_quote: This study characterized a male infertile patient suffering from azoospermia and a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family.

paragraphs.text: Dong et al. (2021) studied 9 women with primary infertility from 7 independent families. In the first pedigree, 2 sisters had recurrent hydatidiform moles. The other 7 patients, from 6 families, had embryonic arrest or recurrent implantation failure. They were identified by screening patients with embryonic arrest, recurrent implantation failure, or recurrent pregnancy loss.

paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) described a 32-year-old Chinese woman (F1_II:4) who had had primary infertility for 4 years. She had regular menses and normal ovarian reserve. Her husband's semen and the karyotypes of both partners were normal. She had 22 mature oocytes. The 8 fertilized by ICSI became 3PN or PPN embryos. With conventional IVF, 5 oocytes formed normal 2PN embryos and 3 became 3PN/PPN embryos. None of the 2PN-derived embryos formed blastocysts, whereas 2 of 3 3PN/PPN-derived embryos from ICSI developed into late-stage blastocysts.

paragraphs.text: In 9 infertile women from 7 families, Dong et al. (2021) identified 5 novel biallelic mutations in the MEI1 gene by whole-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation. Two of the mutations were found in the pedigree in which 2 sisters had recurrent hydatidiform moles. paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in 20 women from Guangzhou, China, who had a high rate of abnormal fertilization during ICSI. Two of the 20 women had biallelic MEI1 variants, and all 4 variants were novel. The proband of family 1 was compound heterozygous for a c.622T-C transition in exon 6, predicted to cause a ser208-to-pro (S208P) substitution, and a c.2647C-T transition in exon 21, predicted to cause an arg883-to-ter (R883X) substitution. Both were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The proband of family 2 was compound heterozygous for a c.3037T-G transversion in exon 24, predicted to cause a trp1013-to-gly (W1013G) substitution, and a deletion of exons 21 to 31. The deletion is given as c.2546_3525del in the text and as c.2546_3825del in the table and discussion. Because the deletion spans c.3037, the family 2 proband appeared homozygous for c.3037T-G. The copy-number loss was confirmed by qPCR. Functional studies in HEK293T cells gave mixed results. The R883X variant increased MEI1 mRNA but reduced MEI1 protein, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay. The W1013G variant increased MEI1 protein levels. Neither the S208P variant, which was classified as of uncertain significance, nor the exon deletion altered protein expression.

paragraphs.text: Wu et al. (2024) studied embryos from their MEI1-mutant patient by whole-genome sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing. Two day-3 cleavage-stage embryos and 2 day-6 blastocysts were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomies and trisomies. Global methylation levels in the 2 blastocysts were 0.344 and 0.168, far outside the optimal window of 0.25 to 0.27. paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) also performed RNA-seq on 3 day-3 embryos from the family 1 proband and compared them with control embryos. They found 2,005 downregulated and 1,904 upregulated genes. The downregulated genes were enriched for the meiotic cell cycle and for epigenetic regulators, including histone demethylases and deacetylases. Maternal-effect genes were dysregulated, and qPCR confirmed reduced expression of MEI1, MKI67, ASTL, and WEE2. The authors proposed a dual mechanism. In one arm, the meiotic and mitotic cell cycles and genomic stability are impaired. In the other, dysregulated epigenetic processes disrupt zygotic genome activation.
